The task: fix compilation errors in the test file. Likely there are many duplicate imports, missing semicolons, etc. Let's examine.

The error: line 17 import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource missing semicolon. Indeed after that line there is no semicolon. Need to add ;.

Also there are duplicate imports and unused imports though they don't cause compile errors (duplicates allowed? duplicate import statements are okay, but there are duplicate import lines. Might cause warnings but fine.

But also there is both JUnit 4 @Test and JUnit 5 imports; they used org.junit.Test (JUnit4) and org.junit.jupiter.api.Test (JUnit5). In current code they imported org.junit.jupiter.api.* earlier, and also org.junit.Test. The code uses @Test annotation from JUnit5? It uses org.junit.jupiter.api.Test imported via wildcard. But also there is line `import org.junit.Test;` which maybe conflicts? Both annotations have same name but ambiguous. The compiler will error: The @Test annotation is ambiguous because both org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and org.junit.Test are imported. That will cause compilation error. Need to remove import org.junit.Test; and possibly use fully qualified if needed. The test methods they wrote use @Test from JUnit5; they also used @DisplayName, @ParameterizedTest, etc all JUnit5. So remove JUnit4 import.

Also duplicate imports: org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments imported twice, and org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest imported twice, etc. Duplicate imports are okay but not issue. But also duplicate import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith imported twice. Duplicate but okay.

However they also imported org.mockito.* twice.

But biggest compile errors: missing semicolon after MethodSource import line, and duplicate @Test import ambiguous.

Let's also verify other potential errors: they used InOrder and inOrder static method? In test spyVerification_delegationCalledOnce they use `InOrder inOrder = inOrder(barSeries, spyManager);`. That requires import static org.mockito.Mockito.inOrder; or import org.mockito.InOrder; The code only imported org.mockito.* and static org.mockito.Mockito.* which includes inOrder? Yes static import includes all static methods from Mockito, including inOrder method. So fine.

But we need to import org.mockito.InOrder? Not necessary because they use InOrder type. static import doesn't import type. However they imported `import org.mockito.*;` which includes InOrder (since InOrder is in org.mockito). So okay.

Potential error: method run of BarSeriesManager: we see they call manager.run(strategy, TradeType.BUY) etc. That's method defined in BarSeriesManager. Should compile.

The test uses @AfterEach and Mockito.reset with many arguments; there is duplicate resetting of manager maybe okay.

Provide final corrected file.

Let's rewrite imports cleanly: include needed imports only.

Imports needed:

org.junit.jupiter.api.Test, DisplayName, BeforeEach, AfterEach, ExtendWith
org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest
org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments
org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource
org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.* static import
org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments (already)
org.mockito.Mock, Mockito, InOrder, etc
static org.mockito.Mockito.* (including verify, when, etc)
org.ta4j.core.BarSeries
org.ta4j.core.Strategy
org.ta4j.core.TradingRecord
org.ta4j.core.num.Num
org.ta4j.core.Trade.TradeType

Also maybe need import java.util.stream.Stream.

Also import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension.

Ok.

Also have duplicate fields: oneAmount and amountOne both refer to same? Not used many. It's fine.

Now adjust code: remove duplicate manager initialization lines: They assign manager = Mockito.spy(new BarSeriesManager(barSeries)); twice. Keep one.

Also in @AfterEach reset list duplicate manager arguments; fine but maybe not needed. Keep.

But need to adjust imports to avoid duplicate ambiguous Test.

Let's produce corrected code.
